Official page (sydney.edu.au/scholarships) confirms the VCIS is an automatic-consideration, university-wide coursework merit scholarship for any CRICOS-registered bachelor or coursework master, with no application required. Award is nominated by a committee of two nominees of the Executive Director, Sydney Future Students and one nominee of the Admissions Office; no professor, research group or degree-specific faculty is associated. No supervisor or program-faculty professor could be identified on official sources.

Official page (uwa.edu.au) confirms the Global Excellence Scholarship is an automatic ATAR/WAM-based tuition discount awarded by UWA Admissions, applicable to any eligible undergraduate or postgraduate coursework course. No named professor, research group, lab or programme director is associated with the award; enquiries are directed to the Future Students Centre (askUWA). No supervisor entries are invented.

Official page (monash.edu) confirms the Monash International Leadership Scholarship is an automatic-consideration undergraduate tuition scholarship for holders of an unconditional Monash course offer, with no separate application, awarded across all undergraduate degrees. No named professor, academic unit, research group or programme director is tied to the award on the official page; no other official Monash page links a supervising professor to this scholarship.

The Hubert H. Humphrey Fellowship Program is a U.S. Department of State (Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs) national programme, administered by the Institute of International Education, as stated on the official site: 'The Humphrey Program is funded by the U.S. Department of State and administered by the Institute of International Education.' It is a non-degree fellowship with no single attached institution; host universities vary by cohort and placement is arranged by the programme, so no supervising professor can be verified. Per instructions, national/government schemes with no attached institution are not applicable.

Official page (admissions.miami.edu) confirms the Stamps Scholarship is an undergraduate merit award selected through holistic admission review (Early Decision I / Early Action) with no separate application. Support is provided by the Office of Academic Enhancement's Premier Scholar Initiatives, which lists only professional advising staff (Associate Director and Program Manager) and no professors; the only published email is the admissions office contact admission@miami.edu. No named supervising professor or faculty research group is tied to the award.
